newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU environment ministers discuss emission levels.
newsitem.headline: EU environment ministers discuss emission levels.

text.p: European Union environment ministers began an informal session of talks on Sunday aimed at striking a deal to cut EU countries' collective emissions of carbon dioxide and other greenhouse gases by the year 2010.

EU diplomats were downbeat about the prospects of a final decision from the closed-door session, unusually scheduled on Sunday evening ahead of formal EU ministerial meetings on Monday and Tuesday and international talks by climate negotiators starting on Monday in Bonn.
"They are not going to decide anything today, it's only informal," one EU diplomat told Reuters as the meeting started.

Ministers' talks centre on a plan drawn up by Dutch Environment Minister Margreet de Boer to cut EU emissions of greenhouse gases by 15 percent of their 1990 levels by the year 2010 and to share out the burden of proposed cuts.
The plan targets a series of greenhouse gases, those thought by scientists to cause warming of the world's climate by trapping solar energy in the atmosphere.
It would hit hardest in Luxembourg, Germany, Austria and Denmark, which would have to cut gas emissions by 40, 30, 25 and 25 percent respectively by the 2010 deadline.
A 20 percent cut is foreseen for Britain, 15 percent for Belgium and 10 percent for Finland, Italy and the Netherlands.
France, meanwhile, would face cuts of five percent while increases of five percent would be allowed for Greece, Sweden and Ireland, 15 percent for Spain and 25 percent for Portugal.

The Netherlands, which holds the EU presidency, based its plan on an assessment of the 15 EU countries' energy economies and hopes to break the bloc's so-far fruitless efforts to forge an EU-level deal to take to world-wide talks intended for conclusion in Kyoto, Japan, next December.
